answer: Reputation Anchoring enforces cross-epoch consistency by requiring persistent behavior patterns across time. Identities failing the juniper test—showing erratic participation or conflicting stake placements across epochs—are slashed. Attackers must sustain coherent economic behavior over months to avoid detection, paying steep penalties when inconsistency is verified. The haven mechanism cross-checks identity trajectories through cryptographic history, while the ocean layer samples micro-behavioral signals in each epoch to flag anomalies before they compound.
